THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORAL JUDGMENT

Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties,
they are taken up for final disposal.

2. These appeals are filed by the claimants challenging common judgment & award dated 24.02.2016 passed in MVC No.228/2011 & MVC No.230/2011 by the Additional District & Sessions Judge, Gadag (for short, 'the Trial Court') being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation and praying for higher compensation.

3. Brief facts of the case necessary to adjudicate these appeals are that the appellant/claimant in MVC No.228/2011 (MFA No.102331/2016) filed claim petition seeking compensation for the injuries suffered by him and the appellants/claimants in MVC No.230/2011 (MFA No.102333/2016)
filed claim petition seeking compensation for the death of their father viz., Shivappa Karadi.

In the claim petition filed by them, they stated that, on 30.12.2010 the appellants/claimants and one Mr.
Shivappa Karadi, after attending a marriage ceremony, were proceeding in NC: 2024:KHC-D:11341 a Tempo Trax bearing registration No.KA-37/7743.
The driver of the said tempo trax drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle resulting in occurrence of the accident.
It is stated that, due the said accident, the claimant in MVC No.228/2011 suffered grievous injuries, and Mr.Shivappa Karadi suffered injuries and died on spot.
Hence, claim petitions were filed by the injured claimant and the legal representatives of the deceased Mr. Shivappa Karadi seeking compensation.

4. On issuance of notices, the respondents - owner and insurer of the Tempo Trax entered appearance and opposed the claim petition denying the age, occupation and income of the injured claimant and that of the deceased Mr.Shivappa Karadi.
The Trial Court recorded evidence of the parties.

The claimants examined four witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.4 and produced 49 documents,
which were marked as Exs.P.1 to P.49.
The respondents did not adduce any evidence.
The Trial Court, along with other claim petitions, by common judgment and award, on 24.02.2016 awarded total compensation of Rs.2,19,100 in MVC No.228/2011 and Rs.5,18,000/- in MVC No.230/2011.
Being NC: 2024:KHC-D:11341 aggrieved by the same, the claimants are before this Court seeking for higher compensation.

5. Sri. Chandrashekhar M.Hosamani, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant in MFA No.102331/2016 submits that the injured claimant is an Advocate by profession and sustained Basavaraj vs Tulasappa on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155462588/
3 serious fractures; however, the Trial Court without considering the evidence available on record has awarded a meager compensation of Rs.2,19,100/- which requires to be re-assessed.
Insofar as MFA No.102333/2016 is concerned, learned counsel submits that the appellants/claimants lost their father Mr.Shivappa Karadi in the accident.

The deceased Mr.Shivappa Karadi was aged about 50 years as on the date of the accident and his income was at Rs.4,500/- notionally which is on the lower side and the same needs to be enhanced by taking the income at an higher rate and also by awarding 'loss of future prospects of the deceased'.
He submits that the compensation awarded by the Trial Court is not in consonance with the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
Hence he seeks to reassess the compensation and to grant higher compensation by allowing the appeals.
Per contra, Sri. Nagaraj C.Kolloori, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-insurance company in the above appeals supports the impugned judgment and award.
Insofar as MVC No.228/2011 is concerned, learned counsel submits that the claimant is an Advocate by profession and his avocation is continued even after the accident.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Trial Court is just and proper and does not call for any interference.

Insofar as MVC No.230/2011 is concerned, learned counsel submits that the claimants have not produced any evidence with regard to income and hence, the Trial Court has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/-
per month, notionally, and further the compensation awarded under all heads is just and proper which does not call for any modification.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss both the appeals.
7. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for respondent- insurance company.
Perused the material available on record.
The only point that arise for consideration in the above appeals is i) Whether the injured claimant/legal representatives of the deceased is/are entitled for enhanced compensation?

It is not in dispute that in the road traffic accident that occurred on 30.12.2010, the claimant in MVC No.228/2011 sustained left frontal fracture, small frontal EDH cross midline, anterior interhemipheric SAH, bifrontal pneumocephalus, Basal cisterns open.
It is not in dispute that the injured is an Advocate by profession and, even after the accident, he has continued with his profession.
Hence, the Trial Court has rightly not awarded any compensation under the head 'loss of future income due to accidental injury'.

However, for the purpose of awarding compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid up period', this Court reassesses the income of the injured claimant at Rs.5,500/- per month, as per the Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, and taking the laid up period as four months.
The amount awarded by the Trial Court under the head 'medical expenses', in a sum of Rs.1,57,110/- is left undisturbed.

This Court having regard to the nature of injuries suffered by the injured claimant and also keeping in mind the fact that the claimant was inpatient in the hospital for a period of twenty days, and the treatment taken by him, reassesses the compensation, to which the injured claimant would be entitled to, as under:

2. Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
3. Diet, transportation & attendant Charges, Rs. 25,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 22,000/-

Thus, the claimant in MVC No.228/2011 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,04,110/- as against Rs.2,19,100/- awarded by the Trial Court.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
9. Insofar as MVC No.230/2011 is concerned, the claim petition is filed by the minor children of the deceased Mr.Shivappa Karadi, through their uncle Mallikarjun @ Mallappa, who is examined as P.W.3.
The evidence available on record indicates that the deceased Shivappa Karadi was aged about 50 years as on the date of the accident and doing agricultural work.

Taking note of the year of accident and placing reliance on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
this Court reassesses income of the deceased at Rs.5,500/- per month notionally.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex NC: 2024:KHC-D:11341 Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Pranay Sethi & Others1, the claimants are entitled to an addition of 10% of the assessed income under the head 'loss of future prospects of the deceased' as the deceased was aged 50 years as on the date of the accident.

Hence, the compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' to which the claimants would be entitled to is worked out as under:
Rs.5,500 + 10% x 12 x 13 x 2/3 = Rs.6,29,200 /-
10.
In view of decision in Pranay Sethi's case referred supra, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- each with 10% escalation under the heads 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.
The claimants are also entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each with 10% escalation under the head 'loss of parental consortium'.

1. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,29,200/-
2. Loss of estate Rs. 16,500/-
3. Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
4. Loss of parental consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
(Rs.44,000 x 3) Total Rs. 7,94,200/-
Thus, the claimants in MVC No.230/2011 are entitled to total compensation of Rs.7,94,200/- as against Rs.5,18,000/- awarded by the Trial Court.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

12. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Trial Court insofar as MVC No.228/2011 is concerned, the same is modified holding claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,04,110 /- as against Rs.2,19,100/-
awarded by the Trial Court.

d) The enhanced compensation amount, in the above claim petitions, shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
e) The respondent-insurer shall deposit the entire compensation amount with accrued interest before the Trial Court within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
f) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per award of Trial Court.
